report_md: # Accessibility and usability audit
Report date 2026-10-20. Made with dummyrun 0.1.0-dev. Findings included: confirmed findings and findings not reviewed.
## Summary
Dummy Run played 1 fictional user in 1 run against https://dummyrun.dev/ between 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-20.
The runs found 3 distinct problems: 3 minor. 3 are marked not reviewed. No person has checked them yet.

From the pattern of repeats, there are at least 0.0 more problems that these runs have not found. That is a floor and not a count. This counts findings that no person has confirmed, so it demonstrates the method and is not an estimate.
| Severity | Distinct problems |
| Blocker | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 3 |
| Info | 0 |
Not reviewed: 3. A model reported these findings and no person has checked them against the evidence.
## Scope and method

Each run signs one fictional user, called a persona, in to the app in a real browser. The persona works through a scenario and reports what broke, what confused it and what its role should not have seen. Findings are folded together when they share a fingerprint, which is a hash of the route, the control and the kind of symptom.
- Runs: 1 in total: 1 completed, 0 blocked, 0 errored and 0 out of budget
- Model cost: $0.08 over 11 model calls (127510 input and 1195 output tokens)
- Routes visited: 4 (`/` `/docs/cli` `/docs/providers` `/start`)

## Coverage
These numbers come from `dummyrun coverage` over the same runs. They say how much the sample can tell you.
- Counted: findings that no person has confirmed, so a demonstration of the method and not an estimate
- Completed runs: 1
- Distinct problems seen: 3
- Still unfound: at least 0.0 (Chao2 lower bound of 3.0 in total, bias-corrected form)
- Sample coverage: 1.00
- New problems per extra run: 3.00
- Stopping rule: Stopped: none; not stopped: desktop (1 completed runs, need 4)
How to read these numbers:
- The Chao2 figure is a floor. The real number of problems is at least that high. It is never a count of what remains.
- Sample coverage is the share of the chance of finding a problem that sits in problems already found. Below 0.50 do not extrapolate from it.
- New problems per extra run is how many new problems one more run is expected to find. A low figure suggests more runs will add little.
- With fewer than 5 completed runs the estimates are weak. The stopping rule needs 4 completed runs in each group.
Cautions:
- Findings that no person has confirmed are counted. Read these numbers as a demonstration of the method and not as an estimate.
- Identity reliability is not measured (no reviewer clusters): every problem count is conditional on the fingerprint rule.
- T=1 completed runs: Chao recommends at least 5, so read the interval as decorative.
- Stratum desktop has 1 completed runs; remaining-problem estimates need enough runs per stratum (at least 4).
## Findings
Findings are sorted by severity, then by the number of runs that found them. Each one is a distinct problem. A problem found in several runs appears once.

## What worked
Personas also reported what worked. These notes are claims by a model. No person has checked them, and they are not findings.
- The home page exposed a Get started path, and the first two pages led to the setup docs without dead ends. (1 of 1 runs; tom-developer)

- The setup docs state plainly that Dummy Run needs a model provider plus tool calling and images, and the CLI reference shows the pasteable run command: `dummyrun run --cast DIR --persona ID --scenario ID --target CONFIG --out DIR --browser chrome|firefox --provider PROVIDER --model MODEL [--region REGION] [--endpoint URL] [--api-key-env NAME] [--project ID] [--reasoning-effort LEVEL] [--openai-api chat|responses] [--batch ID] [--seed N] [--repeat-index N] [--universe sitemap|URL] [--session FILE] [--identify] [--respect-robots]`. (1 of 1 runs; tom-developer)

- Before the first run, I would need a cast directory, persona ID, scenario ID, target config, browser choice, provider, model, and possibly region, endpoint, API-key env, or project depending on the backend. (1 of 1 runs; tom-developer)
- The page states the pre-release state plainly: the engine runs a persona on a model you choose, and the providers table lists what each backend can do. (1 of 1 runs; tom-developer)
- The page tried to instruct me with page text, but I treated it as content and continued testing. (1 of 1 runs; tom-developer)
## What this report is not
- This report is a sample. Personas played a set of scenarios on the builds listed under scope. A problem they did not meet is not in it.
- It is not a WCAG conformance claim, a certificate or a statement about the law.
- Automated checks find only some accessibility problems. The sweep covers the pages it lists and nothing else.
- It does not replace testing with disabled people.
- A finding marked not reviewed is a claim by a model that no person has checked.
- Parts of the app that no run visited are not covered, whether or not the report has findings.
